correctness.rationale: For the repaired files: 2(x+y+1) is the norm difference, so for odd prime powers one first eliminates y and then solves (2x+1)^2=-1; the two split roots are simple, and the inert primes have no roots. Equal parity gives the two mod-2 roots but forces one norm to be 2 mod 4. CRT gives the all-modulus counts. Joint finite valuation laws follow from divisibility and subtraction of tails. For a fixed integer d, one can test exact equality of its local valuations at primes up to Y once Y contains the prime factors of d; the error in this test is at most the probability of any common prime >Y. The union bound of the record is valid because any such prime is <=2N+1; the terms from 1/(Np) and 1/N² vanish. This proves full convergence, with almost-sure finiteness of the limiting product by summable prime activity. Each split-prime mean factor is exactly 1+2/p, whose product diverges; below t=1 the positive-moment factors differ from one by a summable O_t(p^(t-2)), with monotone convergence, and nonpositive powers are bounded. Independent congruence tests through modulus 129 agree. The frozen decimals 0.44742064 and 0.4474206426 lie above even the partial Euler-product upper bound through 10^8. The split-prime truncated product and the all-integer residue tail bound instead bracket the value between about 0.447420610275 and 0.447420612512, so the repaired eight-place value is 0.44742061. The correction does not alter the exact law or moment threshold. The repaired local mass display also explicitly restricts the last two cases to split primes.
residual_risks: The infinite-mean assertion is for G_infinity, not an asymptotic formula for finite-box means.

evidence: In the Gaussian integers the step is 1+i; a common Gaussian prime must divide that step. By contrast a split rational prime may divide one norm via a prime over p and the other via its conjugate. Magness et al. §4 treat divisibility of Gaussian elements on a fixed primitive line. The same step along a fixed line x-y=d has a fixed odd support dividing d²+1, whereas the box spans varying d, including nonprimitive lines.

value.rationale: The nearest diagonal step gives a natural adjacent norm pair rather than arbitrary polynomial parameters. The exact split/inert/ramified spectrum and all its prime-power masses are sufficient to calculate individual gcd probabilities and identify a global infinite first moment even though each local first moment is finite. It is that full arithmetic structure, not the Euler-product decimal or infinite mean in isolation, that is useful beyond the general existence theorem.
